title: Go SDK: stream multiplexing, deadline semantics, and coordinated retry behavior
creator: Asha Patel
description: Improve the Go SDK streaming implementation to support multiplexed stream usage across goroutines, define clear deadline/cancellation boundaries, and coordinate retries without leaking goroutines or double-sending user data. Provide ergonomic consumer-facing examples and a migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: SDK provides stream object that can safely be shared across goroutines for concurrent reads/writes without races
Context deadlines cancel only the active request and do not unintentionally close the shared stream for other in-flight producers/consumers
Automatic retry orchestrator retries idempotent operations and respects user-provided max-deadline, with exponential backoff and jitter
No goroutine or connection leaks observed in stress tests (10k concurrent short-lived streams over 30 minutes)
Examples in repository show recommended patterns: single-writer/multi-reader, demultiplexing responses, and graceful client shutdown
Docs and migration guide published in SDK repo and linked from release notes
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamHandle which wraps the raw transport and exposes Send/Recv methods that accept per-call contexts
Use per-call contexts to bound request lifetimes; StreamHandle maintains a root context for connection lifecycle separate from per-call contexts
Add internal retry coordinator that serializes retry attempts for the same logical message id to avoid duplicate sends when callers concurrently retry
Backpressure: provide non-blocking Send with a bounded buffer and an optional blocking variant. When buffer is full, Send returns an error that callers can use to apply backoff or drop behavior
Telemetry hooks: expose counters for send_failures, retries, aborted_due_to_deadline, and in_flight_messages for Console integration
Tests: unit tests for context propagation, integration tests against a local mock server that simulates long tail latencies and transient 5xx errors
Benchmark: measure p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency with continuous batching enabled vs disabled
api_changes: New type: StreamHandle (methods: Send(ctx context.Context, req []byte) (id string, err error), Recv(ctx context.Context) (Message, error), Close() error)
Deprecate existing BlockingStream.Send which used package-level deadlines (marked deprecated in this release)
Add SendOptions to control idempotencyKey and blockingBehavior (Block|Fail|Drop)
Expose Config fields: MaxBufferedMessages, RetryPolicy, PerCallTimeoutDefault
migration_guide: Old pattern: launching multiple goroutines that call BlockingStream.Send directly can result in connection-level cancellation when any goroutine's context times out
New pattern: create a single StreamHandle per logical conversation and call Send with per-message contexts. Multiple goroutines may call Send/Recv on the same StreamHandle safely
If you relied on implicit timeouts, set PerCallTimeoutDefault or pass explicit contexts to Send to preserve previous behavior
For idempotent operations, populate SendOptions.idempotencyKey to allow safe retries; non-idempotent operations should be classified and use Fail or Drop blockingBehavior
testing_plan: Unit: context cancellation race detectors for concurrent Send/Recv paths
Integration: run against mock server that returns transient 429/500 responses and validate retry coordinator honors idempotencyKey
Load: 10k concurrent clients for 30m using k6/ginkgo harness; check for goroutine count stability and connection count
Chaos: inject network partitions and abrupt server closes to confirm client recovers and reconnects without leaking resources
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: introducing StreamHandle API may break some customers — mitigation: mark prior APIs deprecated and provide adapter shim for 2 minor releases
Risk: retries might double-apply non-idempotent operations — mitigation: require explicit idempotency key; default RetryPolicy is conservative
Risk: bounded buffer causes unexpected drops — mitigation: default to blocking behavior and expose non-blocking Send only behind opt-in flag
work_log: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Asha Patel. Initial proposal sketched and design doc linked.
2025-02-14: Spike completed — implemented prototype StreamHandle that isolates connection lifecycle from per-call contexts. Found race in old BlockingStream when cancelling during flush.
2025-02-17: Design review with runtime and SDK leads. Decided to add per-message idempotencyKey and an internal retry coordinator. Action: Liam to author RFC for retry coordinator.
2025-02-19: RFC posted. Early feedback: prefer explicit buffer limits and opt-in non-blocking sends. Added telemetry requirements.
2025-02-22: PR #8140 opened with initial StreamHandle implementation and unit tests. CI failing intermittently on integration test due to flaky mock timings.
2025-02-24: Fixed race by moving connection closure to a dedicated goroutine with cancellation handshake. Integration tests stabilized locally.
2025-02-26: In Progress — polishing examples and writing migration guide. Planning to target sdk-go-0.9.0
